nodes.summary: A group $G$ is finitely presented in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups if there are a natural number $n$, a finite subset $S$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ letters, and a surjective homomorphism $f \colon F_n \to G$ whose kernel is the relation subgroup of $S$ in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups.
nodes.title: Groups finitely presented in the torsion-free quasivariety

nodes.summary: There is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) that is finitely presented in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups but is not a finitely presented group.
nodes.title: Budkin's theorem (Kourovka Problem 18.17)

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) that is finitely presented in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups but is not a finitely presented group.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.17 (statement)

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F_n$ be the free group on the $n$ letters $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, and let $S$ be a subset of $F_n$. The relation subgroup of $S$ in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups is the intersection of all normal subgroups $N$ of $F_n$ that contain $S$ and satisfy the following: for every $x \in F_n$ and every integer $k \ge 1$, if $x^k \in N$ then $x \in N$.
